title: Surface a risk no one's tracking
why_matters: There's always one risk the team has half-acknowledged in corridor conversations but hasn't put on the RAID log. By week 11, you've heard enough corridor conversation to know what it is. Naming it formally — in writing, with a proposed mitigation — is one of the higher-leverage moves you can make this quarter.
steps: Spend twenty minutes thinking about what worries the team that nobody's said out loud in a planning meeting. Common candidates: key-person dependency, vendor risk, regulatory change, technical debt the team has stopped seeing.
Pick one. Open the RAID log playbook. Write it as a single sentence with concrete impact and likelihood.
Draft a proposed mitigation that costs less than a person-week. If it costs more, it's not a mitigation — it's a separate project.
Bring it to the person who'd own the response. In writing, with the proposed mitigation, and one question: "have I miscalibrated this?".
success_criteria: One previously-untracked risk is documented on the RAID log with impact, likelihood, and a costed mitigation. The relevant owner has received it. The conversation about it is logged.
reflection_prompt: What kept this risk untracked for so long, and is that pattern likely to repeat?
